stories.title: Three Claude Skills I Think Every Org Should Have
stories.summary: An engineering organization becomes more efficient by building executable tools rather than relying on documentation that often becomes stale and misleading. The author recommends three skills: a create-app skill that provisions databases, wires up logging, registers services with identity providers, and deploys to production; a deploy-service skill that integrates forward deploys, rollbacks, environment-scoped tests, and post-deploy smoke tests; and a service-debugging skill that matches live symptoms to known failure patterns.

stories.title: G-Eval, Explained
stories.summary: G-Eval is a prompting framework introduced in a 2023 paper by Yang Liu and colleagues at Microsoft that uses a large language model as a reference-free evaluator of generated text. The framework has three components: a precise rubric defining the evaluation dimension, auto-generated chain-of-thought evaluation steps, and a scoring step. To avoid score collapse onto a single dominant value, G-Eval replaces direct integer scoring with a probability-weighted expectation over the tokens the model assigns to each possible score.

stories.title: AI Workflows Need Topological Sort
stories.summary: AI workflows are fundamentally dependency problems where consumer steps cannot execute before producer steps finish. Directed acyclic graphs model these workflows as nodes and directed edges, while topological sort produces a valid execution order. Kahn's algorithm computes this ordering in O(V+E) time, and because nodes at the same level share no dependencies, they can execute in parallel — a key advantage over linear pipelines.
